title: Contemporary Health Issues
source_note: Standard Nigerian university GST health-education curriculum: communicable and non-communicable diseases, reproductive and maternal health, nutrition, mental health, substance abuse, environmental sanitation, first aid, and public health issues relevant to Nigeria.

questions.question: The World Health Organization (WHO) defines health as:
options: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity
The absence of any diagnosed illness
The ability to work and earn a living
questions.correct_answer: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity
questions.explanation: The WHO's classic 1948 definition explicitly extends health beyond the absence of disease to physical, mental, and social well-being.

questions.question: Malaria is caused by which type of organism?
options: A protozoan parasite of the genus Plasmodium
questions.correct_answer: A protozoan parasite of the genus Plasmodium
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.question: Which mosquito genus transmits malaria?
questions.correct_answer: Anopheles
questions.explanation: The female Anopheles mosquito is the vector responsible for transmitting the malaria parasite to humans.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most widely used method for preventing mosquito bites at night in malaria-endemic areas like Nigeria?
options: Sleeping under an insecticide-treated bed net
questions.correct_answer: Sleeping under an insecticide-treated bed net
questions.explanation: Insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) are a core, evidence-based intervention for reducing mosquito bites and malaria transmission.

questions.question: Tuberculosis (TB) primarily affects which organ, though it can spread to others?
questions.correct_answer: The lungs
questions.explanation: TB is primarily a pulmonary disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, though extrapulmonary TB can occur.

questions.question: How is tuberculosis mainly transmitted from person to person?
options: Airborne droplets from coughing or sneezing
questions.correct_answer: Airborne droplets from coughing or sneezing
questions.explanation: TB spreads when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or speaks, releasing bacteria-containing droplets into the air.

questions.question: Cholera is primarily transmitted through:
questions.correct_answer: Contaminated water or food
questions.explanation: Cholera, caused by Vibrio cholerae, spreads mainly via the fecal-oral route through contaminated water or food.

questions.question: A key symptom of cholera that can lead to rapid death if untreated is:
options: Severe watery diarrhea causing rapid dehydration
questions.correct_answer: Severe watery diarrhea causing rapid dehydration
questions.explanation: Cholera causes profuse watery diarrhea that can lead to life-threatening dehydration within hours if not treated with rehydration.

questions.question: Typhoid fever is caused by which organism?
questions.correct_answer: Salmonella typhi (a bacterium)
questions.explanation: Typhoid fever is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, usually spread through contaminated food or water.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-communicable (lifestyle) disease?
questions.correct_answer: Hypertension
questions.explanation: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is a non-communicable disease linked to lifestyle, diet, and genetic factors, not an infectious agent.

questions.question: Hypertension is generally defined as a persistently elevated blood pressure of approximately:
questions.correct_answer: 140/90 mmHg or higher
questions.explanation: Blood pressure consistently at or above 140/90 mmHg is the traditional clinical threshold used to diagnose hypertension.

questions.question: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is primarily characterized by:
options: The body's cells becoming resistant to insulin, leading to high blood sugar
Complete absence of insulin production from birth
A viral infection of the pancreas
questions.correct_answer: The body's cells becoming resistant to insulin, leading to high blood sugar
questions.explanation: Type 2 diabetes is mainly driven by insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency, often linked to obesity and lifestyle factors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major modifiable risk factor for many non-communicable diseases (e.g., heart disease, diabetes)?
questions.correct_answer: Unhealthy diet and physical inactivity
questions.explanation: Diet and physical activity are lifestyle factors that individuals can change, unlike fixed factors like age or genetics.

questions.question: Obesity is most commonly assessed using which measure?
questions.correct_answer: Body Mass Index (BMI)
questions.explanation: BMI, calculated from weight and height, is the standard screening tool used to classify underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obesity.

questions.question: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) primarily attacks which cells of the body?
options: CD4 (T-helper) cells of the immune system
questions.correct_answer: CD4 (T-helper) cells of the immune system
questions.explanation: HIV targets and destroys CD4 T-cells, progressively weakening the immune system's ability to fight infections.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common mode of HIV transmission?
options: Casual contact such as hugging or sharing utensils
Mother-to-child transmission during pregnancy or birth
questions.correct_answer: Casual contact such as hugging or sharing utensils
questions.explanation: HIV is not spread through casual contact; it requires exchange of specific body fluids such as blood, semen, or breast milk.

questions.question: AIDS stands for:
questions.correct_answer: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome
questions.explanation: AIDS is the advanced stage of HIV infection, in which the immune system is severely damaged.

questions.question: Which practice is most effective at reducing the sexual transmission of HIV and other STIs?
options: Consistent and correct use of condoms
questions.correct_answer: Consistent and correct use of condoms
questions.explanation: Condoms act as a barrier that significantly reduces the risk of transmitting HIV and other sexually transmitted infections.

questions.question: Gonorrhea and syphilis are both examples of:
questions.correct_answer: Sexually transmitted bacterial infections
questions.explanation: Gonorrhea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae) and syphilis (Treponema pallidum) are both bacterial STIs.

questions.question: Stigma toward people living with HIV/AIDS most significantly contributes to:
options: People avoiding testing and treatment due to fear of discrimination
questions.correct_answer: People avoiding testing and treatment due to fear of discrimination
questions.explanation: Stigma discourages individuals from seeking HIV testing, disclosure, and treatment, undermining public health efforts.

questions.question: Family planning primarily aims to help individuals and couples to:
options: Decide the number and spacing of their children
Eliminate the need for maternal healthcare
questions.correct_answer: Decide the number and spacing of their children
questions.explanation: Family planning enables individuals and couples to make informed choices about childbearing, including timing and spacing.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a modern contraceptive method?
questions.correct_answer: Oral contraceptive pills
questions.explanation: Oral contraceptive pills are a modern, medically recognized method of preventing pregnancy.

questions.question: Antenatal care refers to:
options: Healthcare given to a woman during pregnancy
questions.correct_answer: Healthcare given to a woman during pregnancy
questions.explanation: Antenatal (prenatal) care involves regular medical checkups during pregnancy to monitor the health of mother and baby.

questions.question: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended by health authorities for approximately how long after birth?
questions.correct_answer: The first 6 months
questions.explanation: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding (no other food or liquids) for the first six months of an infant's life.

questions.question: Immunization works primarily by:
options: Stimulating the immune system to produce protective antibodies against a specific disease
Killing bacteria already present in the bloodstream
Providing vitamins to boost general health
Physically blocking pathogens from entering the body
questions.correct_answer: Stimulating the immune system to produce protective antibodies against a specific disease
questions.explanation: Vaccines introduce a weakened, inactivated, or partial form of a pathogen so the immune system learns to recognize and fight it.

questions.question: Which of these diseases is preventable through routine childhood immunization?
questions.correct_answer: Measles
questions.explanation: Measles is a viral disease that is preventable through routine childhood vaccination, unlike the listed non-communicable conditions.

questions.question: A balanced diet should generally include:
options: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water in appropriate proportions
questions.correct_answer: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water in appropriate proportions
questions.explanation: A balanced diet supplies all essential nutrient classes in proportions that meet the body's needs.

questions.question: Kwashiorkor is a form of malnutrition primarily caused by a deficiency of:
options: Protein, despite often adequate calorie intake
questions.correct_answer: Protein, despite often adequate calorie intake
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor results from severe protein deficiency and classically presents with edema (swelling), even when caloric intake is not extremely low.

questions.question: Marasmus is a severe form of malnutrition resulting from:
options: Overall severe deficiency of both calories and protein
questions.correct_answer: Overall severe deficiency of both calories and protein
questions.explanation: Marasmus results from an overall energy (calorie) and protein deficit, leading to severe wasting.

questions.question: A diet lacking sufficient iodine can lead to which health condition?
questions.correct_answer: Goiter (enlarged thyroid gland)
questions.explanation: Iodine is essential for thyroid hormone production; deficiency causes the thyroid gland to enlarge, forming a goiter.

questions.question: Vitamin A deficiency is a well-known cause of:
questions.correct_answer: Night blindness
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is essential for vision, particularly in low-light conditions; its deficiency commonly causes night blindness.

questions.question: Mental health is best described as:
options: A state of well-being in which a person can cope with normal life stresses, work productively, and contribute to their community
The complete absence of any negative emotion
A condition only relevant to people with diagnosed mental illness
The ability to avoid all forms of stress
questions.correct_answer: A state of well-being in which a person can cope with normal life stresses, work productively, and contribute to their community
questions.explanation: Mental health, per WHO, is a broader concept of well-being and functioning, not merely the absence of mental disorder.

questions.question: Depression is best classified as:
options: A common mental health disorder marked by persistent sadness and loss of interest in activities
A normal, brief reaction to a single bad day
A purely physical illness with no psychological component
questions.correct_answer: A common mental health disorder marked by persistent sadness and loss of interest in activities
questions.explanation: Depression is a recognized mental health disorder characterized by persistent low mood, loss of interest, and other symptoms lasting weeks or longer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a healthy way to help manage stress?
options: Regular physical exercise and adequate sleep
questions.correct_answer: Regular physical exercise and adequate sleep
questions.explanation: Exercise and sufficient sleep are evidence-based, healthy strategies for managing and reducing stress.

questions.question: Substance abuse refers to:
options: The harmful or hazardous use of psychoactive substances such as drugs or alcohol
The prescribed use of medication under medical supervision
questions.correct_answer: The harmful or hazardous use of psychoactive substances such as drugs or alcohol
questions.explanation: Substance abuse specifically denotes use that causes harm to physical or mental health, distinct from appropriate medical use.

questions.question: Chronic tobacco smoking is a well-established major risk factor for which disease?
questions.correct_answer: Lung cancer
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoke contains numerous carcinogens, and smoking is the leading preventable cause of lung cancer.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes drug addiction (dependence)?
options: A chronic condition characterized by compulsive drug use despite harmful consequences
A temporary preference for a particular drug
A condition that only affects a person's physical appearance
questions.correct_answer: A chronic condition characterized by compulsive drug use despite harmful consequences
questions.explanation: Addiction involves compulsive substance-seeking and use, continuing despite negative consequences, due to changes in brain function.

questions.question: Which of the following is generally classified as a 'hard drug' commonly associated with substance abuse concerns in Nigeria?
questions.correct_answer: Cocaine
questions.explanation: Cocaine is a powerful stimulant drug and a controlled substance widely recognized as a hard drug with high abuse potential.

questions.question: Environmental sanitation primarily involves:
options: Practices that keep the environment clean and free from conditions that could harm health, such as proper waste disposal
questions.correct_answer: Practices that keep the environment clean and free from conditions that could harm health, such as proper waste disposal
questions.explanation: Environmental sanitation covers waste management, drainage, and hygiene practices that prevent disease-causing conditions in the surroundings.

questions.question: Improper disposal of refuse and stagnant water in the environment is a major contributor to the breeding of:
questions.correct_answer: Mosquitoes
questions.explanation: Stagnant water and poorly managed waste create breeding grounds for mosquitoes, which transmit diseases like malaria.

questions.question: Access to safe drinking water and proper sanitation is important mainly because it helps prevent:
options: Waterborne diseases such as cholera and typhoid
questions.correct_answer: Waterborne diseases such as cholera and typhoid
questions.explanation: Contaminated water is a major transmission route for pathogens causing diseases like cholera and typhoid.

questions.question: First aid is best defined as:
options: Immediate, temporary care given to a person who is injured or suddenly ill before professional medical help arrives
questions.correct_answer: Immediate, temporary care given to a person who is injured or suddenly ill before professional medical help arrives
questions.explanation: First aid is the initial assistance given for an injury or illness until more advanced medical care can be provided.

questions.question: In first aid for a minor bleeding wound, the recommended first step is generally to:
options: Apply direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth
Apply ice directly to the open wound
Leave it completely uncovered and untreated
questions.correct_answer: Apply direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth
questions.explanation: Direct pressure helps control bleeding by promoting clot formation and is a standard first-aid response to open wounds.

questions.question: The recovery position is used in first aid primarily to:
options: Keep an unconscious but breathing person's airway open and prevent choking
Increase a conscious person's heart rate
questions.correct_answer: Keep an unconscious but breathing person's airway open and prevent choking
questions.explanation: The recovery position helps maintain an open airway and allows fluids to drain from the mouth, reducing the risk of choking in an unconscious, breathing casualty.

questions.question: Personal hygiene practices, such as regular handwashing, primarily help to:
options: Reduce the spread of infectious disease-causing germs
questions.correct_answer: Reduce the spread of infectious disease-causing germs
questions.explanation: Handwashing and similar hygiene practices remove pathogens from the skin, reducing transmission of infections.

questions.question: The most effective time to wash hands to prevent disease transmission includes:
options: Before eating and after using the toilet
Only once a day, in the morning
questions.correct_answer: Before eating and after using the toilet
questions.explanation: Handwashing before eating and after toilet use are two of the most critical moments for interrupting fecal-oral disease transmission.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'primary health care' as a public health approach?
options: Essential, accessible healthcare provided close to where people live and work, focused on prevention and basic treatment
Care available exclusively to wealthy citizens
Care limited strictly to emergency situations
questions.correct_answer: Essential, accessible healthcare provided close to where people live and work, focused on prevention and basic treatment
questions.explanation: Primary health care emphasizes accessible, community-based care that addresses most health needs, including prevention and basic curative services.

questions.question: Malaria remains one of the leading causes of illness and death in Nigeria mainly because of:
options: The country's tropical climate favoring mosquito breeding, combined with gaps in prevention and treatment access
A total absence of any health facilities nationwide
The disease being untreatable with any known method
Malaria only affecting animals, not humans
questions.correct_answer: The country's tropical climate favoring mosquito breeding, combined with gaps in prevention and treatment access
questions.explanation: Nigeria's tropical climate supports year-round mosquito breeding, and combined with healthcare access challenges, malaria remains a major public health burden.

questions.question: Community health workers play an important role in Nigeria's health system primarily by:
options: Extending basic health services, education, and referrals to underserved communities
Performing complex surgeries in rural clinics
questions.correct_answer: Extending basic health services, education, and referrals to underserved communities
questions.explanation: Community health workers bridge gaps in access by delivering basic care, health education, and referral services at the grassroots level.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a vector-borne disease?
questions.correct_answer: Malaria
questions.explanation: Malaria is transmitted by a biological vector (the Anopheles mosquito), making it a vector-borne disease.

questions.question: Regular physical exercise contributes to health primarily by:
options: Strengthening the cardiovascular system and helping maintain a healthy body weight
Eliminating the need for a balanced diet
questions.correct_answer: Strengthening the cardiovascular system and helping maintain a healthy body weight
questions.explanation: Exercise improves heart and lung function and helps regulate body weight, both of which reduce risk for many chronic diseases.

questions.question: An oral rehydration solution (ORS) is primarily used to treat:
questions.correct_answer: Dehydration caused by severe diarrhea
questions.explanation: ORS replaces lost fluids and electrolytes, making it the standard first-line treatment for dehydration from diarrheal illness.
